text:
MPC rose modestly today, continuing a sharp recovery from an eight-day low on November 6th. The stock has climbed nearly 12% since then, driven largely by a tightening refining margin story: heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year as winter demand sets in, and US refineries are running at 95.2% capacity with diesel and heating oil inventories at relatively lean levels (103.3 million barrels). For a major refiner like Marathon, higher crack spreads—the profit margin between crude input and refined product output—on heating oil are directly accretive to earnings.

The broader context is that global oil markets have shifted from tight supply (which benefited refiners in September–October) to a looser balance: Russian crude production has rebounded post-sanctions disruption, pushing the market into surplus. This could eventually weigh on refining margins, but the immediate seasonal strength in winter fuels and current low inventories are supporting prices for now.
